worked.name: argon_density
worked.description_before: Charge-state-summed number density of argon ions, including Ar+ through Ar18+ and excluding neutral argon; local and averaged forms share this definition.
worked.description_after: Number density of argon ions across all charged ionization states, excluding neutral argon. It is the general argon-ion concentration shared by its local and spatially averaged forms.
worked.documentation_before:
Argon density is the number of argon ions per unit volume, summed over all ionization stages from singly charged Ar+ through fully stripped Ar18+. Neutral argon is excluded.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{Z=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{Z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the total argon-ion number density, $Z$ is the integer argon charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{Z+}}$ is the number density of argon ions in that charge state.

The definition applies to a local value and to averages over a specified chord or confined plasma volume, including the [line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) and [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density). It is distinct from argon count, which represents an equivalent-electron inventory rather than particles per volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of argon. The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

The charge-state sum is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon-ion number density, $q$ is the positive integer charge-state index, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of argon ions in charge state $q$, and 18 is the atomic number of argon.

The quantity may be specified locally or as a spatial average, with the averaging domain set by the specific form. The [line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) is the average along a specified plasma path, and the [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density) is the average over the confined plasma volume. Both are averages of the local density, not unnormalized line or volume integrals, and both keep the same charge-state-summed ion population.

This quantity is not the argon inventory or count, which is an amount rather than a concentration per unit volume, and it is not an electron density or a density of any other species.

worked.name: ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density
worked.description_before: Ratio of hydrogen-ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing the abundance of ionized protium relative to electrons in the plasma.
worked.description_after: Ratio of hydrogen (protium) ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing the abundance of ionized protium relative to plasma electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of hydrogen-ion number density to free-electron number density at the same plasma location and time. It expresses particle abundance rather than mass-density or charge-density composition.

The local ratio is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{H}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{H}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{H}/e}$ is the hydrogen-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the local [hydrogen-ion number density](name:hydrogen_density), and $n_e$ is the local [free-electron number density](name:electron_density).

The hydrogen population is protium summed over all ionic charge states, consisting only of H+; neutral hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium are excluded. The electron denominator has no imposed thermal or fast-population selection. The ratio is defined where $n_e$ is nonzero and is not the protium fraction of the total hydrogenic population.

No spatial averaging or peak-density time selection is imposed on the underlying ratio. The [volume-averaged hydrogen-to-electron density ratio](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density) averages this local ratio over volume and evaluates it when electron density peaks. That average is distinct from dividing separately volume-averaged hydrogen and electron densities.

The [lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density) is the corresponding species-abundance quantity with lithium ions in the numerator.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of hydrogen (protium) ion number density to free-electron number density. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The underlying local abundance ratio is

$$
R_{\mathrm{H}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{H}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{H}/e}$ is the protium-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the [hydrogen-ion number density](name:hydrogen_density), and $n_e$ is the [free-electron number density](name:electron_density), with both densities evaluated at the same position and time.

The numerator includes all positive charge states of protium, consisting only of singly charged protium ions. Neutral protium, deuterium, and tritium are excluded from the numerator. The denominator must be nonzero. This ratio is not the protium fraction among hydrogenic ions, because its reference population is free electrons rather than hydrogenic ions.

The [volume-averaged member](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density) averages this local ratio over the plasma volume at the time of peak electron density. Averaging the local ratio is not generally equivalent to dividing separately volume-averaged densities; that averaging operation and time selection belong to the child quantity, not the underlying ratio.

The [lithium-to-electron abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density) is the analogous species ratio with lithium-ion density replacing protium-ion density.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

worked.name: ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless abundance ratio of charge-state-summed iron-ion number density to local free-electron number density.
worked.description_after: Ratio of charge-state-summed iron-ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing the local abundance of ionized iron relative to plasma electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the local iron-to-electron abundance ratio in a plasma, comparing the population of iron ions with unbound free electrons.

$$
R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e}$ is the iron-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the total [iron-ion number density](name:iron_density), and $n_e$ is the local [free-electron number density](name:electron_density).

The numerator is summed over all positive iron ionization states, while the denominator counts free electrons and excludes electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions. This is a local ratio with no volume averaging, maximum operation, or specified spatial locus.

The ratio is the iron-specific counterpart of the general [ion-density-to-electron-density ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density); its numerator is the charge-state-summed iron density and its denominator is the electron-density parent quantity.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of iron-ion number density to free-electron number density at the same plasma location and time. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The local iron abundance is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{n_e} = \frac{\sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e}$ is the iron-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density summed over all positive charge states, $n_e$ is the [free-electron number density](name:electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of iron ions with charge number $z$, and $z$ indexes the positive iron charge states from 1 through 26.

Each iron ion contributes once to the numerator, regardless of charge state; neutral iron is excluded. Both densities are local quantities, with no spatial averaging implied. The ratio is defined only when the electron density is nonzero.

Like the [lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density), this quantity expresses unweighted ion-particle abundance relative to free electrons. It is neither a charge-weighted contribution to electron density nor an effective-charge measure.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

worked.name: ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density
worked.description_before: Ratio of charge-state-summed lithium-ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing the abundance of ionized lithium relative to electrons.
worked.description_after: Ratio of an ion species’ charge-state-summed number density to free-electron number density, expressing particle abundance rather than charge contribution.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of lithium-ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing lithium abundance relative to electrons in the plasma. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The local abundance ratio is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{Li}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Li}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{Li}/e}$ is the lithium-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density summed over all positive lithium charge states, and $n_e$ is the [free-electron number density](name:electron_density).

Both densities refer to the same location and instant, and the ratio is defined only where the electron density is nonzero. The lithium population includes singly, doubly, and triply ionized lithium and excludes neutral lithium. Each lithium ion contributes equally to the numerator regardless of charge state; this is not a charge-weighted contribution to electron density or an effective-charge measure.

Volume averaging this local ratio gives the [volume-averaged lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density), whose stated evaluation time is the electron-density peak. Averaging the local ratio is distinct from dividing two separately volume-averaged densities. The [hydrogen-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density) uses the same particle-abundance definition with hydrogen replacing lithium.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of a specified ion species’ number density to free-electron number density. It compares ion and electron particle populations without weighting ions by their electric charge.

The underlying local abundance ratio is

$$
R_{i/e} = \frac{n_i}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{i/e}$ is the ion-species abundance relative to free electrons, $n_i$ is the specified species’ ion number density summed over all positive charge states, and $n_e$ is the [free-electron number density](name:electron_density).

The two densities refer to the same plasma location and time, and the local ratio is defined only where the electron density is nonzero. Neutral atoms are excluded from the ion population, and each ion counts once regardless of charge state. This abundance is neither a charge-weighted contribution to electron density nor an effective-charge measure.

Species-specific members include the [iron-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density). The [volume-averaged lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density) averages the corresponding local lithium ratio over the plasma volume at the time of peak electron density. That aggregation is an average of local ratios, not a ratio of separately volume-averaged densities; neither its species selection nor its averaging and timing restrictions apply to the general quantity.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.
